text: We will continue to develop Plaid Cymru’s Inspire Wales programme to involve all ages in sporting activity and ensure our people stay fit and healthy.
explanation: This is a negative example from the codebook itself: a straightforward programme commitment (sports participation for fitness and health) with purely instrumental language and no moral vocabulary.

text: Values of respect.
explanation: 'Respect' is explicitly listed in the codebook's definition and clarification (a) as explicit moral vocabulary. Even as a fragment, it directly invokes a moral value.

text: • Waiting lists are not tolerable.
explanation: Clarification (a) lists 'tolerable/intolerable' as explicit moral vocabulary. Declaring waiting lists 'not tolerable' is a normative moral evaluation rather than a neutral performance claim.

text: to ensure an efficient and accessible school bus system for communities across the country.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy goal (efficient, accessible school buses). 'Efficient' is a generic positive adjective, and accessibility here is framed instrumentally with no moral vocabulary.

text: work with stakeholders to ensure ticket prices at sporting events do not unfairly discriminate against people from low socio economic backgrounds.
explanation: Uses explicit moral vocabulary listed in clarification (a): 'unfairly discriminate'. Framing ticket pricing as unfair discrimination against low-income people is a moral evaluation.

text: Much of the UK’s language, culture and way of life has been enriched by successive new arrivals over thousands of years.
explanation: A descriptive, factual-cultural claim that arrivals have 'enriched' the country's language and culture. 'Enriched' is a generic positive adjective; no explicit moral-evaluative language is used.

text: The international evidence is clear:
explanation: An empirical appeal to evidence with no moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: and free prescriptions and eye tests for the over-60s, without means testing.
explanation: A neutral description of a policy instrument (free prescriptions and eye tests, no means testing). No moral-evaluative language.

text: In government, The Nationals will place any money left in this program in the hands of school boards and principals who are best placed to know how and where the priorities for their schools lie.
explanation: An administrative arrangement (devolving funds to school boards and principals) justified on grounds of local knowledge, not moral principle.

text: Revive the National Adult Learning Council and local co-ordinating bodies so that diverse elements of lifelong learning can be linked into one coherent system through which learners can progress.
explanation: A structural/administrative proposal about coordinating lifelong learning bodies. Purely instrumental language.

text: And as I’ve mentioned, as a result of our initiative, the Three Strikes legislation was passed.
explanation: A factual claim that legislation was passed; no moral vocabulary or normative evaluation.

text: and stop unions looking to restrict their freedom to choose how they want to work.
explanation: The clarification states that appeals to freedom/liberty as a value being protected or unjustly restricted are included. The text opposes unions 'restricting their freedom to choose how they want to work'.

text: Every person, however frail or vulnerable, has a place and a purpose in this world.
explanation: This is a positive example from the codebook: it affirms the inherent worth of every human being, 'however frail or vulnerable' — a direct moral claim about human dignity.

text: Ensure that all children will be tested in literacy and numeracy at two stages during their primary school education.
explanation: A neutral policy instrument (literacy and numeracy testing at two stages). No moral vocabulary.

text: - We have one court system
explanation: A descriptive statement about institutional structure (one court system) with no moral-evaluative language.

text: Many new small businesses are started by women.

text: Our economy will be thriving, delivering balanced growth with jobs that last in every nation and region.

text: courts and tribunals that are independent of the government of the day.
explanation: A description of an institutional arrangement (independent courts and tribunals) with no explicit moral vocabulary or moral imperative.

text: Prioritise the development of high-standard affordable homes by amending and expanding the use of Special Development Zones and / or a new permit scheme.

text: and contribute new technology.
explanation: A neutral, instrumental fragment about contributing technology; no moral-evaluative language.

text: / and fast, frequent inner-city services.
explanation: A descriptive fragment about transport services; generic positive adjectives ('fast, frequent') with no moral content.

text: Introduce a competitive new system for how permits are processed for oil and gas exploration.
explanation: An administrative proposal for processing oil and gas permits; 'competitive' is an economic/efficiency frame, not moral vocabulary.

text: Reduce by 50 per cent the rates bills of village shops, pubs and/or garages where they are the last one, two or three remaining in their communities.
explanation: A fiscal policy instrument (rates reduction for remaining village shops). No explicit moral vocabulary; support for rural communities is framed instrumentally.

text: · further support for back country reafforestation.
explanation: A neutral programme commitment (reafforestation support) with no moral vocabulary.

text: We will change the Proceeds of Crime legislation to enable the police to smash organised criminal gangs.

text: Although some schools provide such education, it is essential that all children regardless of the school they attend have access to a proper IT education so as to equip them with the knowledge and practical experience to participate fully in society.

text: Structural adjustment for river communities

text: so as to avoid the cost escalation associated with legal actions being driven into higher courts by inflation.

text: We will introduce a Food Waste Bill, requiring large food retailers and food manufacturers to take steps to reduce food waste,

text: This is improving education for our children.
explanation: A generic positive claim about improving education; no moral vocabulary or normative judgment.

text: Funding the development of a comprehensive range of materials and resources to support teaching through Irish.

text: Provide increased capital investment in visitor attractions and visitor activity facilities.
explanation: A capital investment commitment for tourism facilities; purely instrumental/economic language.

text: Simplifying Tax Compliance: We will allow all companies to base their preliminary corporation tax returns on prior year tax liabilities, reducing their need to hire advisers to estimate their current year tax liabilities before the year is finished.

text: Employment of New Zealanders wishing to work is our first priority.
explanation: A statement of economic policy priority (employment); no explicit moral vocabulary or normative evaluation.

text: Develop individual NZ Inc country strategies to grow our exports with key markets.
explanation: An export-growth strategy; purely economic/instrumental language.

text: playing a constructive role in world events focussed on human rights concerns.
explanation: Clarification (a) explicitly lists 'human rights' as moral vocabulary. Framing the country's world role around human rights concerns invokes a moral concept, even in an instrumental diplomatic context.

text: (E.g. N52/N62 from Dundalk to Limerick, via the Midlands as a strategic road corridor)
explanation: A descriptive reference to a road corridor; neutral infrastructure detail with no moral content.

text: ACT aims to replace violence and poverty amongst Maori with caring and security through education, enterprise and self-discipline.
explanation: Invokes virtues and moral qualities listed in the definition and clarification (b): 'caring' and 'self-discipline', and frames violence and poverty as conditions to be morally replaced with 'caring and security'.

text: Te Tiriti states the  conditions under which  iwi/hapū  and  the  Crown agreed to  co-operate in a unified  nation.
explanation: A descriptive/factual statement about what Te Tiriti states regarding cooperation between iwi/hapū and the Crown; no explicit moral-evaluative language.

text: Introduce new incentives for the provision of Affordable Housing.
explanation: A policy instrument (incentives for affordable housing provision) described neutrally; no moral vocabulary.

text: and ensure adequate support for people with special needs.
explanation: Per the negative clarification, 'special needs' is a descriptive reference to a morally charged subject, and the text is instrumental ('ensure adequate support') with no explicit moral-evaluative language. 'Adequate' is a sufficiency standard, not moral vocabulary.

text: Work with the Regional Tourism Development Boards in conjunction with Local Authorities and the Tourism Industry to develop comprehensive, interactive local area tourism web sites carrying details of all possibilities in an area for tourists and with a booking facility.
explanation: An administrative/economic commitment to develop tourism websites with booking facilities; purely instrumental language.

text: establish comprehensive and transparent reporting requirements.
explanation: A purely administrative commitment (reporting requirements) with no moral vocabulary; fits the negative clarification on neutral descriptions of administrative structures.

text: We will:  Use central government public procurement policy as a tool of local growth and community development, for example by purchasing from diverse sources and using local labour, goods and services,
explanation: Procurement policy framed as a tool of local growth and community development — an economic/instrumental argument with no moral-evaluative language.

text: The qualifications gap between the rich and the poor and between Māori and non-Māori must be closed
explanation: Frames an inequality (the qualifications gap between rich and poor, Māori and non-Māori) as something that 'must be closed' — a moral imperative. This matches clarification (c): an inequality that 'must be closed'.

text: Support Tourism Ireland in coordinating ‘The Gathering 2012’ as a major  initiative to encourage people of irish heritage from all over the world to visit ireland in 2012, with a range of special programmes on offer.
explanation: A descriptive programme commitment about a tourism initiative; instrumental language with no moral vocabulary.

text: New Zealand First has a plan that sets targets towards providing a sound economic base by the year 2020.
explanation: Economic targets and planning ('sound economic base by 2020'); an economic argument with no moral content.

text: Measurement of water quality around New Zealand is inconsistent.
explanation: A factual/empirical claim about inconsistent water-quality measurement; no evaluative or moral language.

text: Their anger is justified.
explanation: Direct moral evaluation — declaring anger 'justified' is a judgment of moral legitimacy. This is a positive example in the codebook.

text: and its highly successful KiwiReach home mortgage deposit subsidy scheme will be extended so that more New Zealanders benefit.
explanation: Programme description with a generic positive adjective ('highly successful'); per the negative clarification, generic positive adjectives without moral content are coded 0.

text: Support community services and volunteers working to combat loneliness, particularly in later life.
explanation: Instrumental programme commitment (services and volunteers to combat loneliness). Although loneliness is a morally significant topic, the text uses no moral-evaluative vocabulary — akin to the negative clarification's descriptive references to vulnerable people.

text: and assist Scotland’s aquaculture sector to become a world leader.
explanation: Economic/sectoral aspiration (aquaculture as 'world leader'); no moral vocabulary.

text: Put greater priority on family reunification, especially the reunion of children with their parents.
explanation: The negative clarification explicitly names 'family reunification' as a descriptive reference to a morally charged subject; the text is instrumental (setting priorities) with no moral-evaluative language.

text: That means renegotiating the EU-IMF deal to include a jobs strategy,
explanation: Economic policy argument (renegotiating a deal to include a jobs strategy); no moral vocabulary.

text: They will soon become the scientists and researchers who make great discoveries, the engineers and mathematicians who build our communities, the doctors and nurses who heal and comfort the sick, the teachers who will educate the next generation, the leaders who transform government, the poets, artists, and writers who entertain and inspire.
explanation: An aspirational vision of children's future professions; although warm in tone, it lacks explicit moral vocabulary and fits the negative clarification on aspirational visions lacking moral-evaluative language.

text: Why are the poor still likely to be children of the poor, / caught in the poverty trap set by poor education, low-skilled jobs and unemployment?
explanation: A rhetorical question framing intergenerational poverty as a wrong demanding explanation and redress ('Why are the poor still likely to be children of the poor, caught in the poverty trap set by...'). The metaphor of a 'trap set by' social conditions frames the issue as a moral wrong (clarification c). Borderline, since it lacks explicit words like 'unjust', but the normative framing goes beyond a statistical claim.

text: Promote supervised after-school activities in schools and a wide range of positive afterschool options for children.
explanation: Programme commitment for after-school activities; instrumental, no moral vocabulary.

explanation: Equality-of-access argument (schools catering for all religions and none) framed purely instrumentally through an administrative process (White Paper); per the negative clarification, such instrumental access arguments are 0 absent explicit moral vocabulary.

text: As our allies in spirit, they ended the Soviet terror that had consumed so many millions more.
explanation: 'Soviet terror that had consumed so many millions' is explicit vice language and moral condemnation; the codebook's clarification (c) specifically cites 'Soviet terror'.

text: The focus will be on providing a stiffer test of what is in New Zealand’s best interests.

explanation: A factual claim about an MP's voting record; no moral vocabulary in the text itself.

text: Cumbersome bureaucracy is preventing children in remote rural areas from accessing any ECE.

text: We’re putting a strong emphasis on early intervention and health promotion.

text: They are paving the way for societies that are free.
explanation: Invokes freedom as a value being advanced ('societies that are free'); the clarification states that appeals to freedom/liberty as a value are included.

text: The Nationals will implement the third stage of AusLink, investing minimum funding of $35 billion.

text: There are as many risks to the health and well being of New Zealanders in ignoring this issue as there are in proceeding hastily.

text: Provide broadband on all islands.

text: and expand its capacity to deliver a range of medical facilities on UN mandated missions.
explanation: Instrumental capacity expansion for medical facilities on UN missions; descriptive/administrative with no moral vocabulary.

explanation: Economic argument linking tax abolition to investment and industry growth; no moral content.

text: Speeding up delivery of the key recommendations in the McIver Report, to support and enhance the Post Leaving Certificate sector.

text: whose plans would gut investments in federally financed labs and universities that build new American industries

text: Development of a land transition plan which will include regulation of farming practices to reduce environmental damage,
